claims.claim: Xcel's Q2 2026 ongoing EPS rose to $0.93 from $0.75 and management reaffirmed 2026 ongoing EPS guidance of $4.04-$4.16.

Xcel has signed agreements aimed at large-load/data-center growth, including a Google data-center electric service agreement in Minnesota and a NextEra MOU covering generation, storage and transmission for large loads.
A GE Vernova strategic alliance reserves five F-class gas turbines and multiple gigawatts of wind-turbine capacity, improving equipment-supply visibility for future generation projects.

risks.risk: Large-load growth requires regulatory approvals and substantial capital while financing costs are rising.

unknowns.unknown: Timing and realized economics of data-center load additions and associated generation buildout remain prospective.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 EPS improvement was primarily driven by increased recovery of electric infrastructure investments.
Year-to-date interest charges increased $174 million, primarily from higher debt levels, showing the financing burden accompanying infrastructure expansion.
Xcel continues to target long-term annual EPS growth of 6%-8+% and annual dividend growth of 4%-6%.

risks.risk: Higher debt and interest expense can dilute benefits from rate-base growth; regulatory outcomes determine recovery timing and returns.

contradictions.contradiction: Infrastructure recovery is lifting earnings while the debt used to fund expansion is simultaneously increasing financing costs.

unknowns.unknown: Final regulatory outcomes and realized returns on pending large-load investments are not yet known.
